page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.r9ae.16xlarge is a memory-optimized virtual server running on the KVM hypervisor. Built on the x86_64 architecture, it is powered by an AMD EPYC 9T95 processor operating at a clock speed of 2.25 GHz. The instance supplies 64 dedicated vCPUs along with 512 GB of total system RAM, establishing an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU density of 8.0 GB per core.

The hardware configuration provides a baseline network throughput of 32 Gbps. No local storage is bundled with the instance, and it does not contain discrete GPU accelerators. Consequently, all persistent storage operations rely on external network-attached volumes, while workloads interact over the available 32 Gbps network fabric.

By delivering a large memory footprint without auxiliary costs associated with local NVMe solid-state arrays or dedicated GPU silicon, the instance offers qualitative cost efficiency for memory-constrained architectures. Tradeoffs include standard CPU clock speeds and complete dependency on remote network storage for disk I/O. Appropriate workloads include in-memory databases, large caching clusters, big data processing engines, and memory-intensive enterprise software deployments.
